evidence.correctness: Since r3 the venture grew from ~23k to 49,655 src lines: a camera-raw developer (DNG, CRW/CR2/CR3, ARW, NEF, ORF, RW2, SRW, PEF, RAF, MRW, DCR, IIQ, 3FR) was added. Recomputed against sources the author did not write. (1) raw_develop._XYZ_D50_TO_SRGB vs Bruce Lindbloom's published Bradford-adapted XYZ(D50)->sRGB matrix: max element difference 2.2e-4 (the code uses the 6-digit 0.412453 primaries; Lindbloom uses IEC-derived ones), D50 white maps to (1,1,1); dc.bradford(D50->D65) equals an independent numpy Bradford to 4.4e-16. (2) cie1931 table at 450/555/560/600 nm equals the CIE 1931 2-degree values (0.3362,0.038,1.77211 / 0.5120501,1,0.00575 / 0.5945,0.995,0.0039 / 1.0622,0.631,0.0008) exactly. (3) xy_to_cct: D65 6503.0 K, illuminant A 2855.8 K, D50 5001.8 K vs published 6504/2856/5003 (Robertson). (4) srgb_encode(0.18)=0.4613561, (0.5)=0.735357, the IEC 61966-2-1 values. (5) decode_lossless_jpeg on streams encoded by ffmpeg's ljpeg encoder (predictors 1,2,3; 97x61x3, random + ramp): 0 mismatches in 17,751 samples each against ffmpeg's own decode. (6) Cull layer: _laplacian_variance 109771.20795021315 / 971.4876 / 8047.4878 vs numpy 4-neighbour Laplacian .var() equal to 1e-12; dhash_hex 9b4c53ce52a79a75 / 0 / 42bc42bcbc42bc42 equals an independent numpy 9x8 area-average left>right hash. (7) analyze_media on ffmpeg solid patches: red 76, green 149, blue 29, grey 128, orange 151 = BT.601 (76.24/149.69/29.07/128/151.38), not BT.709 (54.21/182.38/18.41) - unchanged since r3; exposure red 0.633333 = 1-|76-120|/120 by hand. evidence.fitness: Job: cull a shoot, develop raws, grade and cut deliverables offline. The cull and develop run from a clone with a PYTHONPATH command; no installer, no UI. In my run a frame blurred with a sigma-6 Gaussian at 1200x800 scored sharpness 0.28 and got 2 stars (alternate), not a reject, because analysis runs on a 320x180 downscale: a photographer checks focus at 100% and would reject it. No real shoot has gone through the pipeline and the cull has no photographer's picks to score against (VENTURE.yaml stage prototype). A photographer could use develop as a LibRaw-grade decoder and the cull as a first pass only. 2.
evidence.domain: Raw/colour side compared with the Adobe DNG specification and SDK and colour-science references: Bradford adaptation, ProPhoto/D50 connection space, Robertson CCT, CIE 1931 observer, IEC sRGB curve all match; a colour scientist would sign this half off. Cull side compared with Photo Mechanic/Lightroom practice and ITU-R BT.709: exposure is mean BT.601 luma versus a fixed 120 so saturated colour is mis-weighted (red 76 vs 54) and deliberate low-key frames score as bad; focus is judged on a 320x180 grey downscale so critical-focus misses pass (sigma-6 blur kept as alternate). The product's lead job is the cull, so 2.

defects.what: Exposure grey target (120->100) and sharpness half-point (60->600) can be mutated with every frame_analysis/cull/story test green; the constants that decide keeper vs reject are unpinned. Reported in r1, r2, r3 and now r4.
Cull luma is ffmpeg format=gray, i.e. BT.601 (red 76, green 149) not BT.709 (54, 182), undocumented in code or README; exposure is mean luma vs a fixed 120, penalising low-key frames. Open since r3.
Focus is judged on a 320x180 downscale: a frame blurred with sigma 6 at 1200x800 scores sharpness 0.28 and is kept as a 2-star alternate rather than rejected.

Home page and llms.txt said '12 raw formats'; the formats page said 'Fourteen' and its table lists 15 families; the home-page develop FAQ omitted DCR and IIQ and said only DNG and 3FR need no .dcp. Fixed in the working tree with tests/test_site_format_count.py.

Core colour tests derive expected values from the module's own sRGB primaries matrix, so replacing its Y row with BT.601 passes the four core colour test files.
AGENTS.md says stdlib-only, zero third-party dependencies and no pytest; numpy (incl. LAPACK eigvalsh) is used by raw_develop_np/noise_pca and C is compiled at run time via ctypes.

verdict: Fourth audit; the project more than doubled since r3 by adding a camera-raw developer. That half is strong: the colour matrices match Lindbloom's published Bradford-adapted sRGB matrix to 2e-4, the CIE 1931 table and Robertson CCT match published values, the sRGB curve is IEC-exact, and the lossless-JPEG decoder reproduces ffmpeg-encoded streams with 0 mismatches. The suite is now green (1,445 passed, 0 failed), and the r3 high defect (the page denying rendering) is fixed. It still does not meet the bar: the cull, the product's lead job, has the same two unpinned scoring constants seeded in all four rounds (both survived again), measures exposure in BT.601 not BT.709, and kept a sigma-6 blurred frame as an alternate. The page's raw-format count was stale (12 vs 15; fixed in the working tree with a test) and llms.txt still names a non-installed `shootflow` command. Scores 3/3/2/2/3/2/2.
